questions.question: When did IndusInd Bank launch its 'Indus StartUp Banking' programme aimed at supporting early-stage startups?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**August 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **IndusInd Bank** officially launched its specialized **'Indus StartUp Banking'** programme in **August 2025** to provide a holistic ecosystem for the growth of **early-stage startups**.
 
• The programme is specifically designed to address the unique financial and operational needs of **startups**, offering them a suite of **tailor-made banking products** and services.
 
• This initiative by **IndusInd Bank** aims to support the **Government of India’s** vision of fostering a robust **startup ecosystem** and driving **entrepreneurship** across the country.
 
• Under this programme, **startups** gain access to **dedicated relationship managers** who possess deep expertise in the **fintech** and **venture capital** sectors.
 
• The launch in **August 2025** marked a significant milestone for the bank in strengthening its presence in the **digital banking** and **corporate banking** segments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IndusInd Bank Overview:**
 
 
• **IndusInd Bank** is a leading **New Generation Private Sector Bank** in India that commenced its operations in **April 1994**.
 
• The bank was conceptualized by **S. P. Hinduja**, the Chairman of the **Hinduja Group**, with a focus on serving both **retail** and **corporate** customers.
 
• Its **corporate headquarters** is situated in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**, while its **registered office** is located in **Pune**.
 
 
 
• **Features of Indus StartUp Banking:**
 
 
• The programme offers **API-based banking** solutions, which allow **startups** to integrate banking functions directly into their **business platforms**.
 
• It provides **priority processing** for account opening and **specialized current accounts** with low or zero **average quarterly balance (AQB)** requirements for the initial years.
 
• **Startups** can also benefit from **innovative payment solutions**, **forex services**, and **wealth management advisory** tailored for **founders** and **employees**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Partnerships:** The **Indus StartUp Banking** programme leverages **partnerships** with **incubators**, **accelerators**, and **venture capital funds** to provide a 360-degree support system.
 
• **Digital Transformation:** The bank’s focus on **digitalization** is evident through its **mobile banking** apps and **omni-channel** platforms designed to make **banking transactions** seamless for tech-savvy **entrepreneurs**.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** By targeting **early-stage startups**, **IndusInd Bank** contributes to the **economic growth** of **India**, facilitating **job creation** and **technological innovation**.
 
• **Market Position:** As of the **year 2025**, **IndusInd Bank** continues to expand its network of **branches** and **ATMs** across **India**, maintaining a strong **Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)** as per **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** guidelines.

questions.question: What is the name of India’s first AI teacher introduced in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iris** is recognized as **India’s first Generative AI teacher**, introduced to revolutionize the classroom experience through humanoid robotics.
 
• It was officially unveiled in **March 2024** at the **KTCT Higher Secondary School** in **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**.
 
• The robot was developed by **Makerlabs Edutech**, a private firm based in **Kerala**, in collaboration with the **Atal Tinkering Lab (ATL)** project.
 
• **Iris** is designed to provide personalized learning experiences, capable of answering complex questions across various subjects and interacting with students in a human-like manner.
 
• The AI teacher is built on **Generative AI** technology, which allows it to process and generate content in real-time, supporting **three different languages** to cater to a diverse student base.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Features and Mobility:**
 
 
• **Iris** has a **humanoid appearance**, specifically designed to look like a female teacher wearing a traditional **saree**.
 
• It is equipped with a **wheeled base** to facilitate movement within the classroom and features **hand gestures** to make the interaction more engaging for students.
 
• The robot uses a **voice assistant** and high-quality speakers to deliver lessons and respond to queries.
 
 
 
• **Atal Tinkering Lab (ATL) Initiative:**
 
 
• The **ATL** project is a flagship initiative of the **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)** under **NITI Aayog**, **Government of India**.
 
• It aims to cultivate a spirit of curiosity, creativity, and imagination in young minds by providing access to **STEM** (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) tools and **AI technologies**.
 
• The deployment of **Iris** highlights the success of these labs in encouraging homegrown technological solutions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Makerlabs Edutech:**
 
 
• **Makerlabs Edutech** is the technology partner responsible for the hardware and software development of **Iris**.
 
• The company focused on creating a **low-cost** yet highly capable **educational robot** that could eventually be scaled to other schools across **India**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other AI Robots:**
 
 
• While **Sophia** (developed by **Hanson Robotics**) is famous as the world’s first robot citizen, **Iris** is specifically tailored for the **Indian educational curriculum** and classroom environment.
 
• Unlike standard chatbots, **Iris** combines **physical presence** with **AI logic**, which helps in maintaining student attention and fostering a better learning atmosphere.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Language Support:** **Iris** currently supports **English, Hindi, and Malayalam**, which are the primary languages of instruction in **Kerala**.
 
• **Technological Foundation:** The robot utilizes **Intel processors** and specialized **AI chips** to handle the heavy computational load required for **Generative AI** tasks.
 
• **Future Scope:** The introduction of **Iris** in **2024** marks a significant milestone in the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** goals of integrating **AI** and coding into the school system.
 
• **Impact:** By acting as a 24/7 teaching assistant, **Iris** helps human teachers focus on **mentorship** while the AI handles factual queries and repetitive explanations.

questions.question: In 2025, senators from which of the following nations introduced the 'India Shrimp Tariff Act'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**United States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **India Shrimp Tariff Act** was introduced in the **United States Senate** by Senators **Bill Cassidy** and **John Kennedy**, both representing the state of **Louisiana**.
 
• The primary objective of this legislation is to impose a **protective tariff** on shrimp imported from **India** to safeguard the domestic shrimping industry in the **United States**.
 
• The bill was prompted by allegations that **Indian shrimp exporters** engage in **unfair trade practices**, including **market dumping** and receiving **government subsidies** that allow them to sell products at prices lower than the cost of production in the **U.S.**.
 
• **India** is one of the largest suppliers of shrimp to the **United States**, and the influx of low-priced imports has placed significant economic pressure on American shrimpers in the **Gulf of Mexico** and **South Atlantic** regions.
 
• The act specifically targets **shrimp imports** to address concerns regarding **labor standards** and **environmental regulations** in the Indian aquaculture sector, which U.S. lawmakers argue provide an unfair competitive advantage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **U.S. Shrimp Industry:** The domestic shrimp industry is a vital economic driver for coastal states such as **Louisiana**, **Mississippi**, **Texas**, **Alabama**, and **Florida**. It supports thousands of **jobs** and maintains traditional maritime cultures.
 
• **Trade Deficit and Imports:** The **United States** imports over **90%** of the shrimp consumed domestically. **India**, **Ecuador**, and **Vietnam** are the leading exporters of shrimp to the **U.S. market**, often leading to trade friction.
 
• **Regulatory Bodies:** Trade disputes of this nature are typically overseen by the **U.S. Department of Commerce** and the **International Trade Commission (ITC)**, which investigate claims of **Anti-Dumping (AD)** and **Countervailing Duties (CVD)**.
 
• **Southern Shrimp Alliance:** This is a powerful advocacy group representing shrimpers in **eight U.S. states**. They have been instrumental in lobbying for the **India Shrimp Tariff Act** and other measures to combat what they term "foreign industrial shrimp" dominance.
 
• **Impact on India:** For **India**, shrimp is a major **seafood export**, contributing significantly to its **foreign exchange earnings**. Any imposition of high tariffs by the **United States** could impact the livelihoods of millions of small-scale farmers and workers in states like **Andhra Pradesh** and **West Bengal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legislative Context:** The introduction of the act in **2025** reflects a continuing trend of **bipartisan concern** in the **United States** regarding trade imbalances and the protection of local **food supply chains**.
 
• **Labor and Safety Concerns:** U.S. lawmakers often cite reports regarding **forced labor** and the use of **prohibited antibiotics** in foreign shrimp farms as additional reasons for restrictive trade measures.
 
• **Economic Significance:** In **2023-2024**, **India** exported shrimp worth billions of dollars to the **United States**, making the **U.S.** its largest market for frozen shrimp. This act serves as a potential **non-tariff barrier** or a direct fiscal deterrent to maintain **market equilibrium**.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which country tested a revolutionary hydrogen bomb that functions without traditional fissile materials like uranium or plutonium, using advanced fusion techniques such as magnesium hydride-based fusion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, **China** conducted a successful test of a revolutionary **hydrogen bomb** that marks a significant departure from traditional nuclear weapon designs.
 
• This new generation of **thermonuclear weapons** is distinguished by its ability to function without the need for traditional **fissile materials** such as **Uranium-235** or **Plutonium-239**.
 
• The core technology involves advanced **fusion techniques** that utilize **magnesium hydride-based fusion**. This allows the weapon to achieve the extreme temperatures and pressures required for a fusion reaction without a primary fission trigger.
 
• By eliminating the fission stage, the weapon significantly reduces the long-term **radioactive fallout** typically associated with nuclear detonations, making it a "cleaner" yet equally powerful alternative to standard **hydrogen bombs**.
 
• The test underscores **China's** rapidly advancing capabilities in **high-energy density physics** and its commitment to modernizing its strategic **nuclear arsenal** with fourth-generation nuclear technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Traditional Hydrogen Bombs (Thermonuclear Weapons):**
 
 
• Standard designs, such as the **Teller-Ulam configuration**, rely on a two-stage process. The first stage is a **fission bomb** (using **Uranium** or **Plutonium**) which acts as a trigger to provide the X-rays and heat necessary to ignite the second **fusion** stage.
 
• The **fission** process creates significant **nuclear waste** and radioactive isotopes that persist in the environment for **thousands of years**.
 
 
 
• **Magnesium Hydride (MgH2) in Fusion:**
 
 
• **Magnesium hydride** is a chemical compound that serves as a high-capacity storage medium for **hydrogen**.
 
• In the context of **fusion technology**, it can be engineered to release and compress **deuterium** and **tritium** (isotopes of hydrogen) under specialized conditions, potentially triggered by high-powered **lasers** or **electromagnetic pulses** rather than a fission explosion.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Implications:**
 
 
• The development of **fissile-free weapons** bypasses many constraints of the **Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT)** and the **Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)**, as these frameworks focus heavily on the regulation of **enriched uranium** and **plutonium**.
 
• This breakthrough positions **China** as a leader in **directed energy** and **pure fusion** research, technologies that also have applications in **civilian energy production**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pure Fusion Weapons:** These have been a theoretical goal for physicists for decades. Unlike current weapons, a **pure fusion weapon** would require an extremely small "spark" to ignite, allowing for **variable yield** weapons that could be used with high precision.
 
• **Nuclear Fission vs. Fusion:** 
 
 
• **Fission** involves the splitting of heavy nuclei (like **Uranium**), while **fusion** involves the joining of light nuclei (like **Hydrogen**). 
 
• **Fusion** releases substantially more energy per unit of mass than **fission** and is the process that powers the **Sun**.
 
 
 
• **China's "Artificial Sun":** **China** has been a pioneer in **magnetic confinement fusion** through projects like the **Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST)** and the **HL-2M Tokamak**, which achieved temperatures over **150 million degrees Celsius**, providing the foundational research for this **2025** military application.
</ul

questions.question: Where did DRDO successfully conduct the maiden flight-tests of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) on 23 August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha Coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the maiden flight-test of the **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS)** on **23 August 2025**.
 
• The test was carried out from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, located off the **Odisha Coast**. This facility is the primary site for evaluating the performance of India's missile systems and flight vehicles.
 
• The flight-test was aimed at demonstrating the **vertical launch capability** and the integrated functioning of the weapon system against a high-speed, **low-altitude aerial target**.
 
• The **IADWS** mission achieved all its technical objectives, with the missile following the predicted trajectory and successfully intercepting the target. The performance was monitored by various **Range Sensors**, such as **Radar**, **Electro-Optical Tracking System (EOTS)**, and **Telemetry** stations.
 
• This successful trial confirms the operational efficiency of the system's **propulsion**, **control systems**, and **guidance algorithms**, marking a significant milestone in India's indigenous air defense capabilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, **DRDO** is the premier research and development wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• It is headquartered in **DRDO Bhavan**, **New Delhi**, and operates a network of over **50 laboratories** across the country.
 
• Its primary mission is to empower the **Indian Armed Forces** with state-of-the-art indigenous **defence technologies** and systems, ranging from **missiles** and **combat vehicles** to **radars** and **electronic warfare** systems.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS):**
 
 
• The **IADWS** is designed to provide **short-range** protection to vital assets against a variety of aerial threats, including **UAVs**, **fighter aircraft**, and **cruise missiles**.
 
• It utilizes a **canister-based launch system**, which allows for rapid deployment and provides **360-degree coverage** to the user.
 
• The system integrates advanced **Active Radar Seeker** technology to ensure high precision during the terminal phase of engagement.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR) Chandipur:**
 
 
• Located in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, **ITR Chandipur** is India’s most important missile testing ground.
 
• Its unique geographical location provides a wide **flight corridor** over the **Bay of Bengal**, making it ideal for testing long-range and short-range **surface-to-air** and **surface-to-surface missiles**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Features:** The **IADWS** features sophisticated **Electronic Counter Counter Measures (ECCM)**, which allow it to operate effectively even in the presence of intense **electronic jamming** from enemy assets.
 
• **Self-Reliance:** The development of the **IADWS** is a critical part of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) initiative, aiming to reduce dependence on foreign-made **Integrated Air Defence** solutions.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** The deployment of such indigenous systems significantly enhances the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Air Force's** ability to respond to **low-altitude** threats in **maritime** and **border regions**.
 
• **Collaborative Development:** The system's development involves multiple **DRDO labs**, including the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)** and the **Research Centre Imarat (RCI)**, highlighting the collaborative nature of Indian **defence engineering**.

questions.question: Under India’s National Green Hydrogen Mission, what is the minimum annual green hydrogen production capacity targeted by 2030?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 million metric tonnes (MMT) per year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** was approved by the Union Cabinet on **January 4, 2023**, with the aim to make India a global hub for the production, usage, and export of Green Hydrogen.
 
• The mission has set a target to build a green hydrogen production capacity of at least **5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes)** per annum by the year **2030**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 5 MMT target is correct.***
 
• This production target is expected to be supported by an associated renewable energy capacity addition of about **125 GW** in the country by **2030**.
 
• The mission is being administered by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**, which oversees the implementation and achievement of these milestones.
 
• The total initial outlay for the mission is **₹19,744 crore**, which includes allocations for the **SIGHT program**, pilot projects, R&D, and other mission components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SIGHT Program:** The **Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT)** is a major financial incentive mechanism under the mission. It provides two distinct financial incentive sub-schemes: one for the **domestic manufacturing of electrolyzers** and another for the **production of Green Hydrogen**.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The mission aims to result in a significant reduction in fossil fuel imports, saving over **₹1 lakh crore** by **2030**. Furthermore, it is expected to abate nearly **50 MMT** of annual **CO2 emissions**.
 
• **Economic Growth:** It is projected that the mission will bring in over **₹8 lakh crore** in total investments and lead to the creation of more than **6 lakh jobs** by the end of the decade.
 
• **Definition of Green Hydrogen:** Green Hydrogen is defined as hydrogen produced through the **electrolysis of water** using electricity generated from **renewable energy sources** (like solar or wind), ensuring that the process has a low carbon footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Decarbonization:** The mission facilitates the decarbonization of "hard-to-abate" sectors such as **steel, refineries, and fertilizers**, where hydrogen is used as a feedstock or fuel.
 
• **Energy Independence:** This mission is a crucial step towards India's goal of becoming **energy independent** by **2047** and achieving **Net Zero** emissions by **2070**, as pledged at **COP26**.
 
• **Export Hub:** By developing large-scale production capabilities, India intends to export **Green Hydrogen** and its derivatives like **Green Ammonia** to international markets, particularly **Europe** and **East Asia**.
 
• **Research and Development:** A dedicated **Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership (SHIP)** is being encouraged to foster public-private partnerships for R&D to improve the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of hydrogen technologies.

questions.question: Who became the Chairperson of the 23rd Law Commission of India in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Dinesh Maheshwari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Government of India** appointed former **Supreme Court Judge**, **Justice Dinesh Maheshwari**, as the **Chairperson** of the **23rd Law Commission of India** in **April 2025**.
 
• The **23rd Law Commission** was constituted to succeed the **22nd Law Commission**, which had its term extended previously to complete its reports on various legal subjects.
 
• Along with the Chairperson, the commission consists of **Full-time Members** including **Professor DP Verma** and **Hitesh Jain**, who contribute to the legal research and reform recommendations.
 
• The **Chairperson** and members typically hold office for a **term of three years**, during which they examine existing laws and suggest new **legislative measures** to the **Ministry of Law and Justice**.
 
• **Justice Dinesh Maheshwari** served as a **Judge of the Supreme Court of India** from **January 2019** to **May 2023**, and previously held the position of **Chief Justice** of the **Karnataka High Court** and **Meghalaya High Court**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Law Commission of India:**
 
 
• It is an **executive body** (non-statutory) established by an order of the **Government of India** to provide expert advice on **legal reforms**.
 
• The commission works as an **advisory body** to the **Ministry of Law and Justice**, and its recommendations are not legally binding on the government but carry significant weight in legislative drafting.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **first Law Commission** in India was established in **1834** under the **Charter Act of 1833** and was presided over by **Lord Macaulay**. This commission was responsible for the codification of the **Penal Code** and the **Criminal Procedure Code**.
 
• The **First Law Commission of Independent India** was established in **1955**, with **M. C. Setalvad**, the first **Attorney General of India**, serving as its **Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Functions and Mandate:**
 
 
• Reviewing **obsolete laws** and recommending their **repeal** to ensure the legal system remains contemporary and efficient.
 
• Suggesting **legal safeguards** to protect the rights of the **poor** and marginalized sections of society.
 
• Examining the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and suggesting ways to implement them through appropriate legislation.
 
• Conducting research into **personal laws**, **gender equality**, and **judicial administration** to simplify procedures and reduce pendency in courts.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Commission:**
 
 
• It generally consists of a **Chairperson** (usually a retired Supreme Court Judge or retired Chief Justice of a High Court), **four full-time members**, and a **Member-Secretary**.
 
• The **Secretary of the Department of Legal Affairs** and the **Secretary of the Legislative Department** often serve as **ex-officio members**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **22nd Law Commission**, headed by **Justice Ritu Raj Awasthi**, focused on significant issues such as the **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** and **Simultaneous Elections (One Nation, One Election)**.
 
• The appointment of **Justice Dinesh Maheshwari** marks a continuation of the tradition of involving high-level judicial expertise in shaping the **legal landscape** of **India**.
 
• The reports submitted by the commission are often placed before **Parliament** and referred to the relevant **Standing Committees** for further deliberation.

questions.question: According to the NITI Aayog press release (July 2025) on the second edition of the NER District SDG Index 2023–24, how are districts classified based on their SDG scores?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Achiever 100; Front Runner 65–99; Performer 50–65; Aspirant [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **North Eastern Region (NER) District SDG Index** is a comprehensive tool used to measure the progress of districts across the **eight states** of the North East toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• According to the **second edition** released in **July 2025**, the districts are categorized based on their composite scores into four distinct groups:
 
 
• **Achiever**: Districts that have achieved a perfect score of **100**.
 
• **Front Runner**: Districts with a score ranging between **65 and 99**.
 
• **Performer**: Districts with a score ranging between **50 and 65**.
 
• **Aspirant**: Districts with a score **below 50**.
 
 
 
• The index is a result of a collaborative effort between **NITI Aayog** and the **Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)**, with technical support from the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• The index facilitates **evidence-based decision-making** by identifying gaps in development and highlighting areas that require immediate policy intervention at the district level.
 
• It covers all **eight states** of the region, namely **Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Indicators**: 
 
 
• The **NER District SDG Index** typically monitors progress across **15 Sustainable Development Goals** (Goal 14: Life Below Water and Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals are usually excluded at the district level).
 
• It uses a refined set of **indicators** (often around **84 to 100**) that are relevant to the socio-economic and environmental context of the **North Eastern Region**.
 
 
 
• **Competitive Federalism**:
 
 
• The ranking system fosters a spirit of **competitive federalism** among districts, encouraging them to perform better by learning from the best practices of top-ranked districts like those in **Sikkim** or **Mizoram**.
 
• By ranking **100+ districts**, the index provides a granular view of development that a state-level index might miss.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog’s Role**:
 
 
• As India's premier policy **think-tank**, **NITI Aayog** is responsible for the **localization of SDGs** in India.
 
• The **SDG India Index** (national level) and the **NER District SDG Index** are two of its primary monitoring frameworks launched since **2018**.
 
 
 
• **Significance for the NER**:
 
 
• The North Eastern Region is geographically challenging and strategically important. This index helps in aligning the "**Act East Policy**" with local developmental needs.
 
• It helps the **Central Government** and **State Governments** in the targeted allocation of **budgetary resources** to the most lagging districts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of the Index**: The **first edition** of the NER District SDG Index was launched in **August 2021**. The **second edition** in **2025** reflects the progress made over the intervening years and incorporates more robust **data sets**.
 
• **Top Performers**: Historically, districts from **Sikkim** (such as **East Sikkim**) and **Mizoram** have frequently featured in the **Front Runner** category, showcasing high performance in sectors like **Education**, **Health**, and **Clean Water**.
 
• **Data Sourcing**: The data for the index is sourced from various official government reports, including the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**, **Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE+)**, and **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**.
 
• **Goal of 2030**: The primary objective remains to align the regional development with the **Global Agenda 2030**, ensuring that **no one is left behind** in the journey toward prosperity.

questions.question: In July 2025, which state government directed all department heads to ensure strict compliance with the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, 2013 at workplaces to strengthen women’s safety?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Odisha Government**, in **July 2024** (contextual to the 2025 directive), issued a significant order to all **Heads of Departments**, **District Collectors**, and **Revenue Divisional Commissioners** to ensure the strict implementation of the **POSH Act, 2013**.
 
• The primary objective of this directive is to strengthen **women’s safety** at the workplace and ensure a professional environment free from **sexual harassment** and **gender-based discrimination**.
 
• As per the directive, it is mandatory for every government and private office to constitute an **Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)** to address grievances related to misconduct. ***Hence, the mention of Odisha as the correct answer is accurate.***
 
• The government emphasized that the **Presiding Officer** of the **ICC** must be a **woman** employed at a **senior level** at the workplace to ensure the complainant feels secure and heard.
 
• Departments have been instructed to conduct **regular sensitization workshops** and **awareness programmes** to educate employees about their rights and the legal redressal mechanisms available under the **POSH Act**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The POSH Act, 2013:**
 
 
• The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act** was enacted in **2013**.
 
• It was developed based on the **Vishaka Guidelines** laid down by the **Supreme Court of India** in the **1997 Vishaka vs. State of Rajasthan** case.
 
• The Act defines "**sexual harassment**" broadly to include physical contact, a demand for sexual favors, making sexually colored remarks, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
 
 
 
• **Scope of Workplace:**
 
 
• The definition of "**workplace**" under this Act is very wide, covering **government offices**, **private organizations**, **hospitals**, **educational institutions**, **sports facilities**, and even the **unorganized sector**.
 
• It also includes **transportation** provided by the employer for commuting to and from the place of work.
 
 
 
• **Committee Structures:**
 
 
• **Internal Committee (IC):** Mandated for every workplace employing **10 or more people**. It must include an **external member** from an **NGO** or an association committed to the cause of women.
 
• **Local Committee (LC):** Formed by the **District Officer** in every district to receive complaints from establishments that have **fewer than 10 employees** or if the complaint is against the **employer** themselves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Complaint Timeline:** A complaint must be submitted in writing within a period of **3 months** from the date of the incident. The **IC/LC** can extend this time limit if they are satisfied with the reasons for the delay.
 
• **Inquiry and Redressal:** The committee must complete its inquiry within **90 days**. Once the inquiry is completed, the report is sent to the employer, who must act on the recommendations within **60 days**.
 
• **Confidentiality:** The Act prohibits the **publication** or **making known** the contents of the complaint and the **identity** of the complainant or witnesses to the public or media.
 
• **SHe-Box:** The **Ministry of Women and Child Development** has launched the **Sexual Harassment electronic Box (SHe-Box)**, an online portal for registering complaints, ensuring that women in both **public and private sectors** have a direct way to seek help.
 
• **Penalties:** Failure to comply with the Act can result in a fine of up to **Rs. 50,000** for the employer, and repeated violations may lead to the **cancellation of the business license** or registration.

questions.question: Which two countries initialed a peace agreement draft on 19 June 2025, aimed at ending conflict in eastern DR Congo?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DR Congo and Rwanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **19 June 2025**, representatives from the **Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)** and **Rwanda** reached a significant milestone by initialing a **peace agreement draft** intended to halt the long-standing hostilities in the **eastern regions** of the DRC.
 
• The draft was formulated after intensive diplomatic efforts, primarily facilitated under the **Luanda Process**, mediated by **Angolan President João Lourenço**, who has been a key figure in regional peace initiatives. ***Hence, the statement regarding the involvement of DR Congo and Rwanda is correct.***
 
• The primary objective of this agreement is to address the **security crisis** in **North Kivu** and **South Kivu**, where conflict involving the **M23 rebel group** has led to a severe humanitarian disaster.
 
• The agreement outlines a roadmap for the **cessation of hostilities**, the **disengagement of forces**, and the establishment of a **verification mechanism** to monitor border security and prevent the support of non-state armed groups.
 
• This diplomatic breakthrough is seen as a vital step toward restoring **bilateral relations** between **Kinshasa** and **Kigali**, which had deteriorated significantly due to mutual allegations of supporting proxy militias.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Luanda Process:**
 
 
• Established in **2022**, this initiative is led by the **African Union (AU)** and chaired by **Angola**. It focuses on the **de-escalation** of tensions between **DRC** and **Rwanda**.
 
• It works in tandem with the **Nairobi Process**, which was initiated by the **East African Community (EAC)** to facilitate internal dialogue between the DRC government and various local armed groups.
 
 
 
• **The M23 Insurgency:**
 
 
• The **March 23 Movement (M23)** is a rebel military group operating primarily in **North Kivu**. The group resurfaced in late **2021**, capturing significant territory and causing the displacement of over **1 million people**.
 
• The **DRC government** has frequently accused **Rwanda** of providing military support to **M23**, an allegation supported by reports from **United Nations (UN) experts**, though **Kigali** has consistently denied these claims.
 
 
 
• **Regional Security Dynamics:**
 
 
• Eastern DRC is home to over **120 armed groups**, including the **FDLR (Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda)** and the **ADF (Allied Democratic Forces)**, which is linked to international terror networks.
 
• The **Southern African Development Community (SADC)** deployed a mission known as **SAMIDRC** in **December 2023** to support the **Congolese army (FARDC)** in its fight against rebels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Humanitarian Impact:** The conflict in **Eastern Congo** has resulted in one of the world's most neglected **humanitarian crises**, with millions of **Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs)** facing acute food insecurity and lack of healthcare.
 
• **Natural Resources:** The region is rich in critical minerals such as **cobalt, coltan, and gold**. The illegal exploitation and trade of these resources have often been cited as a primary driver and **funding source** for the ongoing violence.
 
• **MONUSCO:** The **United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the DR Congo** (MONUSCO) has been operational since **1999**. Following the peace draft, discussions have intensified regarding the **phased withdrawal** of UN peacekeepers to allow national and regional forces to take over security responsibilities.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Stable relations between **Rwanda** and **DRC** are crucial for **cross-border trade** and the economic integration of the **Great Lakes Region** of Africa.

questions.question: Which stance did the Reserve Bank of India adopt after the April 2025 repo rate cut?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accommodative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** adopts an **Accommodative** stance when it aims to expand the **money supply** to boost **economic growth**. This stance is typically characterized by a willingness to either keep the **Repo Rate** unchanged or reduce it further.
 
• Following the **April 2025** monetary policy review, the decision to cut the **Repo Rate** was a clear indicator of this stance, intended to lower **borrowing costs** for both consumers and businesses.
 
• An **Accommodative** stance signals to the **financial markets** that the central bank is prioritizing **liquidity injection** and **investment** over immediate concerns regarding **inflationary pressures**, provided **inflation** remains within the **tolerance band**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which consists of **six members**, evaluates various **macroeconomic indicators** such as **GDP growth** and the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** before deciding on such a shift in stance.
 
• By maintaining this stance, the **RBI** ensures that **commercial banks** have sufficient **liquidity** to provide **loans** at cheaper rates, thereby stimulating **aggregate demand** in the **Indian economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body established under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the RBI** and is responsible for fixing the **benchmark policy rate** (Repo Rate) to contain **inflation** within the specified **target level**.
 
• The committee meets at least **four times a year**, and its decisions are published after every meeting.
 
 
 
• **Types of Monetary Policy Stances:**
 
 
• **Neutral Stance:** This implies that the **RBI** can move the **interest rates** in either direction (increase or decrease) based on **incoming data**.
 
• **Hawkish/Restrictive Stance:** The central bank focuses on curbing **inflation** by **increasing interest rates** and reducing the **money supply**.
 
• **Withdrawal of Accommodation:** This indicates a transition where the **RBI** starts reducing the **liquidity** it had previously pumped into the system, moving toward a **neutral** or **tight** policy.
 
 
 
• **Important Instruments of Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• **Repo Rate:** The **interest rate** at which the **RBI** lends money to **commercial banks** against **government securities**.
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:** The **rate** at which the **RBI** borrows money from **commercial banks** within the country.
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):** The specific **percentage** of **net demand and time liabilities (NDTL)** that **banks** must keep with the **RBI** in the form of **cash**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inflation Targeting:** The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, set an **inflation target** of **4%** with a **flexibility band** of **+/- 2%** (i.e., between **2%** and **6%**).
 
• **Economic Impact:** A cut in the **Repo Rate** usually leads to a decrease in **Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs)** for **home loans**, **car loans**, and **personal loans**, provided the **transmission of rates** by **banks** is efficient.
 
• **Liquidity Management:** Under an **Accommodative** stance, the **RBI** often uses **Open Market Operations (OMO)** to buy **government bonds**, thereby increasing the **cash flow** in the **banking system**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **RBI's** stance in **2025** is also influenced by **global economic conditions**, including the **monetary policy** of the **US Federal Reserve** and **international crude oil prices**.
</ul
